newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy back to Belarus, with tough message.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy back to Belarus, with tough message.

text.p: The United States sent its ambassador back to Belarus on Tuesday with a tough message about the Minsk government's "abysmal human rights record."

Ambassador Ken Yalowitz, who was recalled to Washington on March 25 for consultations amid worsening relations between the two countries, was headed back to Minsk, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Yalowitz was carrying a message about Washington's "serious reservations about the situation in Belarus, particularly its abysmal human rights record," Burns said. "We are informing the government of Belarus that the future course of our relationship depends on its actions, not on its statements."

Washington has repeatedly condemned what State Department spokesmen call the "authoritarian" policies of President Alexander Lukashenko, who has clamped down on opposition to his rule and on those opposed to his closer union with Russia.

The U.S. envoy intended to intensify conversations and meetings with those in Belarus who were interested in "democracy, in human rights, in normal state to state relations, and economic reform," Burns said.

"We can't say with all due candor that we're hopeful for an improvement in U.S.-Belarussian relations, but we're determined to send a signal of our strong support for democracy and strong opposition to dictatorship," the spokesman said.
In March, Washington cut off $40 million in aid because of Minsk's human rights record.
